title: Kill a running process by its name
summary: Use pkill to stop a program that is running but not responding or needs to be closed. It finds all processes matching the name and sends them a termination signal.

steps.explain: Send the default termination signal to all processes matching the given name. This is the standard way to ask a program to close.

placeholders.name: PROCESS_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the process to kill (e.g., firefox, code, spotify)

alternatives.explain: Force kill the process immediately if it ignores the standard signal. The process cannot block this signal.

placeholders.name: PROCESS_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the process to force kill

alternatives.explain: Kill only the oldest process with that name. Useful for closing the main browser window without killing child processes.

placeholders.name: PROCESS_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the process to kill

rollback.explain: There is no direct command to undo a kill. You must restart the application manually if you closed it by mistake.

warnings: Force killing (-9) can cause data loss if the application was saving files. Use the standard signal first.
Be careful with process names; pkill matches substrings, so 'kill chrome' might kill other processes containing 'chrome'.
